subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: StrataScale — mixed GPU pool sizing
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@stratascale.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-06-10T16:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: StrataScale — initial sizing questions

Hi Alex / Nadia,

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, we want to prepare a dedicated capacity proposal that balances cost and performance for the StrataScale production rollout. To put together a recommended SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) and a conservative slot plan, can you please confirm the following by EOD Tuesday (Jun 12)?

- Percent of traffic that is embeddings vs text generation vs reranking (rough %).
- Typical request size (tokens in / tokens out) and 95th percentile latency SLO for API calls.
- Peak concurrent requests and expected sustained qps in a business hour.
- Share any sample traces or the attached workload CSV (CSV format you can drop in reply).
- Whether you plan to use context windows > 8k tokens and approximate % of requests that hit long context (16k/32k).
- Any hard constraints: regional residency, encryption/KMS requirements, audit frequency.

I've attached an SLA draft (SLA-draft-v1.pdf) so legal/ops can flag any must-haves early. Once we have the workload samples, Dev will sketch a slot mix and Priyom will run an initial cost vs latency sensitivity model.

Goal: get a recommended pool and fallthrough strategy (e.g., H100 for long-context + A100 for blended throughput + L4 for cheap embeddings) and a short list of tradeoffs to review on a call the week of June 24.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.inference
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SLA-draft-v1.pdf]

From: Alex Moreno <alex@stratascale.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-06-11T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: StrataScale — initial sizing questions

Lauren — thanks, attaching the CSV with per-endpoint payloads and a short profiling note. Quick answers below:

- Traffic mix (rough): embeddings 60%, generation 30%, reranking/others 10%.
- Typical request: embeddings avg input 128 tokens resulting vector 1536 dim; generation median 120 tokens in, 220 tokens out.
- 95th pct latency target: 250 ms for embeddings; 700 ms for mid-size generation calls (we can accept relaxed latencies for very long contexts).
- Peak concurrent: 1,200 concurrent requests across endpoints in US region; sustained qps ~450 during business hours.
- Long context usage: 10% of calls touch 32k context; another ~15% touch 16k.
- Security: must support customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit logs for the last 90 days.

Timeline: We'd like a budgetary proposal and recommended pool mix by June 22 so internal procurement can start approvals.

Attaching: stratascale_workload_samples.csv (sampled week) and a short runbook note.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of ML Platforms, StrataScale
alex@stratascale.com

[Attachments: stratascale_workload_samples.csv]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@stratascale.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-06-12T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: StrataScale — initial sizing questions

Alex / team — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick back-of-envelope mapping against our perf profiles. High level recommendation below; I'll follow up with a small workbook (capacity_model_v1.xlsx).

Summary recommendation (budget-aware, reliability-first):
- Mix: 40% A100 (fp16 / 8-bit quantized gen), 35% H100 (for 32k/long-context stateful sessions), 25% L4 (cheap, burstable embedding pool).
- Rationale: Embeddings are 60% of tokens but have high qps and tight latency targets. L4 gives best tokens-per-dollar for dense embeddings at 1536 dims when using 4-bit quantized kernels and small batch sizes. A100 is cost-effective for mid-length generation (120/220 tokens) where throughput matters; we can run larger batching for non-interactive work. H100 we reserve for sessions that require 32k context and KV cache retention — memory capacity and NVLink topology matter there.

Sizing sketch (initial slots / steady-state):
- Embeddings (L4 pool): target 200 L4 slots (expect ~650 qps if autoscale burst enabled; this covers 60% embeddings at p95 latency ~200 ms with small batching).
- Generation (A100 pool): target 80 A100 slots sized for 120/220 token median; supports batching to lower unit cost. Expected sustained throughput ~300 qps gen.
- Long-context (H100 pool): target 20 H100 slots for pinned sessions requiring 32k KV cache + memory headroom. This is conservative to avoid eviction and to preserve latency SLO for those sessions.

Operational notes / fallbacks:
- Autoscale policy: keep dedicated baseline as above and allow burst to shared/spot-backed pool for spikes with queued slow-path fallback.
- Quantization: Recommend 4-bit quantization for L4 embeddings pipelines; for generation models run mixed precision on A100 with option to push to H100 for very large contexts.
- KV cache and prefix caching: enable prefix caching for common prompt prefixes to shave 20-30% token compute on generation-heavy endpoints.
- Multi-region failover: deploy primary in us-east with a hot standby in us-west for a subset of capacity (region ask from Alex).

Estimated monthly cost (ballpark, excl. discounts):
- L4 pool: $XXk/month (200 slots, optimized embedding kernels)
- A100 pool: $YYk/month (80 slots)
- H100 pool: $ZZk/month (20 slots)
(Will fill exact numbers in the workbook once Priyom runs cost delta per qps / tokens).

Action items:
- Priyom: run cost sensitivity for +/-20% traffic and provide token-dollar curves.
- Hannah: ops runbook and SLO mapping, include KMS and audit logging steps.
- Lauren: confirm procurement timeline (Alex asked for budgetary by Jun 22).

If this looks reasonable I'll convert to a short executive one-pager and we can present to StrataScale procurement.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.inference

[Attachment: capacity_model_v1.xlsx (stub)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex@stratascale.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: StrataScale — initial sizing questions

Thanks Dev — this is a clear starting point. Operational items I will own:

- Confirm H100 topology constraints (we need NVLink pairings for the 32k KV cache behavior) and verify the requested 20 slot baseline provides the expected KV residency for multi-session workloads.
- Draft an SLO table mapping to the SLA-draft-v1.pdf and call out which endpoints map to dedicated vs fallback.
- KMS/audit: outline steps to onboard customer-managed keys and confirm log retention meets 90-day audit ask.
- Run a failover smoke test plan for cross-region burst to ensure stateful sessions degrade gracefully (plan attached as an ops checklist in the workbook).

Next steps: Priyom, please share the cost curves by EOD June 18 so Lauren can produce a budgetary summary. Lauren, I can join the June 22 review with StrataScale to walk ops constraints.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference

[Attachment: SLA-draft-v1.pdf (referenced), capacity_model_v1.xlsx (ops checklist tab referenced)]
